```{r setup, include=FALSE}
source("dashboard-setup.R")
```

rvis builds complete [shiny](https://shiny.posit.co/) apps from a configuration: a YAML or JSON
file, or an R list. The configuration lists the **items** of the dashboard (inputs, outputs and
containers), how they are laid out, and their **services**: the R code that makes the content of
each output or runs when an input changes. You do not write the user interface and server
functions of the app yourself.

This guide explains the main ideas. The other dashboard guides go further:

| Guide | Content |
|:---|:---|
| [Layouts](dashboard-layouts.html) | Pages, rows and columns, sidebars, tabs, navigation bars, shinydashboard pages and clothes |
| [Item reference](dashboard-reference.html) | Every item type and its settings, the server environment, reactive values, dynamic interfaces, tooltips, modals, guided tours, login and synced tables |
| [Gallery](dashboard-gallery.html) | Apps of the Shiny gallery rebuilt from YAML, and two large showcase dashboards |
| [Shiny packages](dashboard-extensions.html) | Packages of the Shiny ecosystem that rvis supports, and the ones it could support |

## A first dashboard

This YAML file describes a page with a slider and a histogram:

```{r, echo=FALSE}
show_yaml("hello")
```

It comes with rvis as an example. `rvisDashboard()` reads it and returns a `DASHBOARD` object,
which runs as a shiny app:

```{r, eval=FALSE}
library(rvis)
dash <- rvisDashboard(rvisDashboardExample("hello"))
dash$run()                     # or: runDashboard(rvisDashboardExample("hello"))
```

```{r, echo=FALSE}
show_shot("hello")
```

`dash$app()` returns the shiny app object (for example to deploy it in an `app.R` file),
`dash$dashboard.ui()` and `dash$dashboard.server()` return the user interface and the server function.

## The parts of a configuration

| Field | Meaning |
|:---|:---|
| `name` | Name of the dashboard. |
| `layout` | The item (or items) making the page, usually one page container like `fluidPage`, `sidebarLayout`, `navbarPage` or `dashboardPage`. |
| `items` | The items, by name. The name of an item is its shiny id: input `bins` is `input$bins` in the services. |
| `prescript` | R code run at the start of each session, for example to define reactive expressions and functions used by the services. |
| `objects` | Objects copied into `session$userData` of each session. |
| `values` | Initial values of the reactive list `sync` of each session. |
| `observers` | R code run in `observe()` in each session. |
| `settings`, `messages`, `loginTable` | Settings, messages and users of dashboards with a login item. |

Every item has a `type`. There are three kinds of items:

* **inputs** (`textInput`, `selectInput`, `sliderInput`, `actionButton`, ...) take their label from `title`.
  Their optional `service` is run when the input changes.
* **outputs** (`textOutput`, `plotOutput`, `tableOutput`, `dataTableOutput`, `highcharterOutput`, ...)
  show the result of their `service`, which is run again whenever an input or reactive value it
  uses changes. A `static` item shows fixed content (`html`, or any shiny tag as `object`).
* **containers** (`fluidPage`, `sidebarLayout`, `tabsetPanel`, `box`, `bsModal`, ...) hold other
  items, given by name in their `layout`.

Any item can also have a **cloth**: a box, value box, column, well panel or tab panel wrapped around it
without defining a container item, and a **tooltip**, **popover** or **tutor lesson** (guided tour).

## Services

A service is R code, written as text in the configuration. It is evaluated in the server function
of the session, where these objects are available:

| Object | Meaning |
|:---|:---|
| `input`, `output`, `session` | The usual shiny objects. |
| `sync` | Reactive list of the session, with the initial `values` of the configuration (and the synced tables). |
| `report` | Reactive list reporting the state of synced tables (edits, filters, selections). |
| `session$userData` | The `objects` of the configuration, copied for the session. |
| `items`, `settings`, ... | The fields of the dashboard. |
| `hideItems()`, `showItems()`, `enableItems()`, `disableItems()`, `updateItem4Session()` | Methods of the dashboard (see the [reference](dashboard-reference.html#methods)). |

Multi-line services use the YAML block scalar `|`:

```yaml
  plot:
    type: plotOutput
    service: |
      d <- mtcars[mtcars$cyl == input$cyl, ]
      plot(d$wt, d$mpg)
```

Reactive expressions used by several services are defined in the `prescript`:

```yaml
prescript: |
  selected <- reactive(mtcars[mtcars$cyl == input$cyl, ])
items:
  plot:  {type: plotOutput, service: plot(selected()$wt, selected()$mpg)}
  table: {type: tableOutput, service: head(selected())}
```

## YAML, JSON or R lists

**R values in YAML.** Values tagged `!expr` are R expressions, evaluated when the file is read:

```yaml
  variable:
    type: selectInput
    title: Variable
    choices: !expr names(mtcars)
```

**Named choices.** A YAML mapping gives choices with labels (label: value):

```yaml
    choices: {Normal: norm, Uniform: unif}
```

**Text and logical values.** rvis reads YAML with YAML 1.2 rules: only `true` and `false` are logical
values. Words like `yes`, `no`, `y` or `n` stay text, so items can be named `n` or `y`.
Quote values that contain a colon followed by a space (`title: "Number of bins:"`), and do not put
R code containing commas in a flow mapping like `{type: actionButton, service: f(a, b)}`: use the
block form instead.

**JSON.** The same configuration can be a JSON file (without `!expr` values). In JSON, a list
of one item name (`["a"]`) is read as the name itself: write a column of one item as
`{"items": "a"}` in layouts.

**R lists.** The configuration can also be an R list. Fields given to `rvisDashboard()` are added to
the configuration, which is useful to pass R objects:

```{r, eval=FALSE}
dash <- rvisDashboard(list(
  layout = "page",
  items  = list(
    page = list(type = "fluidPage", title = "Hello", layout = list("n", "hist")),
    n    = list(type = "sliderInput", title = "Observations", min = 10, max = 500, value = 100),
    hist = list(type = "plotOutput", service = "hist(rnorm(input$n))"))))

# a YAML configuration with objects from the R session:
dash <- rvisDashboard("my-dashboard.yml", objects = list(sales = my_sales_table))
```

The original R interface still works: `new("DASHBOARD", items = items, king.layout = list("page"))`.

## The examples

rvis comes with `r nrow(rvisDashboardExample())` example dashboards:

```{r}
ex <- rvisDashboardExample()
ex[, c("name", "group", "title")]
```

* **basics**: one feature each, used in the [layouts](dashboard-layouts.html) and [reference](dashboard-reference.html) guides;
* **gallery**: apps of the [Shiny gallery](https://shiny.posit.co/r/gallery/) rebuilt from YAML (see the [gallery](dashboard-gallery.html));
* **showcase**: two large dashboards combining most features.

Run any of them with `runDashboard(rvisDashboardExample("<name>"))`, and copy their files to start your own:

```{r, eval=FALSE}
file.copy(rvisDashboardExample("us-states"), "my-dashboard.yml")
```
